meaning: The finite-past horn (SCG I.13 [30]): if the past is finite, something that is now came to be anew, and what comes to be anew has an innovating cause other than itself. Scope: it reaches a cause of some being's origin, not yet a unique or necessary first cause; what that cause is, is left to the other ways. Its premise STMT-PAST-IS-FINITE is a hypothesis (by q.46 a.2 the beginning is held by faith, not demonstration), so the horn is conditional.
